media.alt: Unchanged original examination page 2, preserving source wording, numbering and layout.

questions.answerKey: Crust: Earth’s thin, outer solid rocky layer. Mantle: thick hot rocky layer below the crust, mostly solid but capable of slow flow. Core: innermost metallic region, with a liquid outer core and a solid inner core.
questions.markingGuide: Source guide gives 2.5 marks × 3 = 7.5 for the three named/explained layers. Award 2.5 per correctly named and explained layer. The mantle is not generally a liquid sea; this scientific clarification is independent of the source guide wording.

questions.content: Apart from seasons name any other three effect of revolution

media.alt: Unchanged original examination page 2, preserving source wording, numbering and layout.

questions.answerKey: Annual change in the latitude of the overhead Sun (combined with Earth’s axial tilt); annual changes in day and night length (combined with axial tilt); periodic changes in Earth–Sun distance, including perihelion and aphelion, because the orbit is elliptical.
questions.markingGuide: Source guide gives 1 mark per effect, total 3. Accept the three accurate effects above or valid equivalents. Do not award the guide’s “Eclipses” point without the additional orbital-alignment conditions: eclipses are not a simple annual effect of Earth’s revolution. The explanation is independently checked and does not change the question.

questions.content: List any four consequences of the earth’s position in the solar system.

media.alt: Unchanged original examination page 2, preserving source wording, numbering and layout.

questions.answerKey: Taking “position” to refer to Earth’s orbital location and mean distance from the Sun: (1) solar energy reaches Earth and powers processes such as photosynthesis; (2) incoming solar heating permits generally moderate surface temperatures compared with much closer or more distant orbits; (3) together with suitable atmospheric pressure, these temperatures allow liquid surface water; (4) Earth’s orbital distance around the Sun corresponds to an orbital period of about 365¼ days, giving the year. These outcomes have additional physical conditions; position alone does not guarantee life or create the seasons.
questions.markingGuide: Source guide allocates four points at 2 marks each, total 8. Independent guidance: award 2 for each distinct scientifically correct consequence with an appropriate qualification, up to 8. The four model categories are solar energy, heating, liquid-water conditions, and orbital period. Accept valid alternatives. Do not award the unqualified claim that third-planet position causes seasons; axial tilt combined with revolution is required.

questions.content: There was a debate on the shape of the Earth. As a Geography expert, with the help of diagrams discuss five (5) evidence to prove that the earth is spherical.

media.alt: Unchanged original examination page 2, preserving source wording, numbering and layout.

questions.answerKey: Five defensible examples: (1) Earth casts a curved shadow during a lunar eclipse; draw Sun–Earth–Moon alignment and the curved shadow edge. (2) A ship travelling away disappears hull first; draw a curved sea surface and two ship positions. (3) Circumnavigation returns a traveller to the starting point along a continuous route; sketch a globe and route. (4) Space photographs show Earth’s rounded outline; sketch the observed globe. (5) The visible horizon changes with observer height and Earth’s surface curves; draw observers at two heights with tangent sight lines. The Earth is slightly oblate rather than a perfect mathematical sphere.
questions.markingGuide: Source guide: five points at 3 marks each, total 15. For each distinct valid evidence, award 1 for stating it, 1 for explaining how it supports a rounded Earth, and 1 for a relevant labelled diagram. The source specifically requires diagrams. Accept valid alternatives; do not award unexplained claims as if they were proofs. This independently checked model avoids treating sunrise alone as conclusive evidence.
